root_cause.text: The `rds_ib_send_unmap_op()` function's switch statement failed to handle masked atomic opcodes (`IB_WR_MASKED_ATOMIC_FETCH_AND_ADD` and `IB_WR_MASKED_ATOMIC_CMP_AND_SWP`), causing masked atomic completions to fall through to the default case and return NULL for `rm`, while leaving `send->s_op` set, leading to a NULL pointer dereference when `rds_ib_send_cqe_handler()` later accesses `rm->m_final_op`.
root_cause.evidence: The patch adds two missing case statements (`IB_WR_MASKED_ATOMIC_FETCH_AND_ADD` and `IB_WR_MASKED_ATOMIC_CMP_AND_SWP`) to the switch in `rds_ib_send_unmap_op()` at lines 173-174, allowing masked atomic opcodes to be handled identically to their non-masked counterparts. The CVE description explicitly states that `rds_ib_xmit_atomic()` always programs masked atomic opcodes, but the completion-side switch only handled non-masked opcodes, causing masked completions to fall through to default and return `rm == NULL` while `send->s_op` remains set, which then triggers the NULL dereference in `rds_ib_send_cqe_handler()` at line 282.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add support for masked atomic work request types in the RDS IB send unmapping handler to prevent unhandled cases and ensure proper cleanup of masked atomic operations.
intent_record.what: Added two new case labels (IB_WR_MASKED_ATOMIC_FETCH_AND_ADD and IB_WR_MASKED_ATOMIC_CMP_AND_SWP) to an existing switch statement that handles atomic operation work request types.
intent_record.how: This change extends the switch statement's coverage to handle masked atomic operations in addition to the previously supported non-masked atomic operations. When these new work request types are encountered during send unmapping, they will now follow the same code path as their non-masked counterparts, executing the atomic operation unmapping logic.

This prevents these cases from falling through to the default case and returning NULL for 'rm', which was the direct cause of the NULL pointer dereference vulnerability.

bic_trace_step.reason: The `rds_ib_send_unmap_op()` function introduced in this commit contains the vulnerable construct. The switch statement (lines 88-109) handles `IB_WR_SEND`, `IB_WR_RDMA_WRITE`, `IB_WR_RDMA_READ`, `IB_WR_ATOMIC_FETCH_AND_ADD`, and `IB_WR_ATOMIC_CMP_AND_SWP` opcodes, but notably DOES NOT handle the masked atomic opcodes `IB_WR_MASKED_ATOMIC_FETCH_AND_ADD` and `IB_WR_MASKED_ATOMIC_CMP_AND_SWP`. When these masked atomic opcodes are encountered, they fall through to the default case (lines 107-111) which only prints a warning and returns NULL for `rm`, while `send->s_wr.opcode` is set to 0xdead (line 112). This leaves `send->s_op` still set with a non-NULL value. Later in the caller `rds_ib_send_cq_comp_handler()` (line 266), the code checks `if (&send->s_op == &rm->m_final_op)` where `rm` is NULL, causing a NULL pointer dereference when accessing `rm->m_final_op`. The fix is not present in this commit - the masked atomic opcodes are simply not handled in the switch statement.
